topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock,op-deployer,kona-sp1: check the SP1 verifier matches the sp1-sdk circuit
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18422

## Why

Every SP1 PLONK proof starts with 4 bytes that identify the circuit it was made with, and the verifier contract rejects any proof whose 4 bytes differ from its own `VERIFIER_HASH()`. Our prover's circuit is decided by the `sp1-sdk` version in `rust/Cargo.toml`; the verifier is decided by an address pinned in op-deployer and `VerifyOPCM`. Nothing connected the two. They agree today only because sp1-sdk 6.3.1 through 6.8.0 all ship circuit v6.1.0. A bump to a new circuit without moving the address would make every `ZKDisputeGame.prove` revert after the proving spend, and nothing would report it.

## What changes for users

Nothing on chain: no bytecode, ABI, or semver change. Three new checks, each in the place that can see the fact it checks:

- `standard.SP1VerifierHash` records the `VERIFIER_HASH()` of the release-approved verifier, next to its address. The sepolia integration test reads the hash from the deployed verifier and holds the constant to the chain, so the address and the hash move together.
- `VerifyOPCM` fails at release when the adapter's verifier returns a different `VERIFIER_HASH()` than the circuit we prove for (`EXPECTED_SP1_VERIFIER_HASH` overrides the constant, like `EXPECTED_SP1_VERIFIER`).
- `kona-sp1-proposer` in network mode refuses to start against a verifier whose hash does not match the circuit its own SDK proves for. It derives that hash from the verification key the SDK ships (`sha256(sp1_verifier::PLONK_VK_BYTES)`), so no proof is generated; that replaces the issue's "first four bytes of a simple proof". The error names both hashes and the SDK circuit, and fails before any game is created or proof is bought. Mock mode logs the hash only, since `MockSP1Verifier` accepts any bytes.

An sp1-sdk bump to a new circuit is therefore caught by the proposer at startup and by `VerifyOPCM` at release, not before merge. A pre-merge link was tried (a JSON pin read by both a Rust test and the Go test) and dropped: it introduced a hand-maintained cross-language data file with no precedent in the repo, for a failure that is loud, early, and harmless on chain.

## Reviewer notes

- The Solidity constant in `VerifyOPCM` is a copy of the Go constant. Solidity cannot read op-deployer (Foundry `fs_permissions` stop at `packages/contracts-bedrock`), so it is held to the chain only when `VerifyOPCM` runs at release, the same as the address constant today. Dismissed the go-code-reviewer note on this for that reason.
- No per-game verifier check before proving: games created before an OPCM verifier swap cannot be proven by the new SDK regardless, and the startup check covers the configured deployment.
- The mocks gain `VERIFIER_HASH()` because they implement `ISP1Verifier`; devstack deploys `MockSP1Verifier` behind `SP1PlonkAdapter`, so the ZK acceptance tests exercise the new adapter and verifier reads with the real proposer binary.
- Review agents run: rust-code-reviewer (clean, two style suggestions applied), go-code-reviewer (lint-go green, no findings retained). No agent covers Solidity; `just pr` passes 16/16 with no snapshot or semver-lock drift.
